one_line: Open on the finished, good-looking result, then show the unboxing in the same room under one held headline.

q1_hook.what: 0:00 a low sweeping pan of a cream living room: foam arches and poufs on a rug, a pink tent at 0:01. No speech. Small thin text: 'Pov: Your baby's favorite play corner is actually beautiful' and 'By Bliss'.
q1_hook.why: The finished, styled corner is the first image and the headline states the promise, answering the worry that baby gear spoils a living room (H1, H2). But the text is small, thin and white on a light picture, hard to read in 3 s (T5, H7), and no voice or face opens it (H4).

beats.what: Two low pans of the finished corner: arches, poufs, a pink tent
beats.why: The result first, with camera movement.

beats.what: A woman and a toddler by a tall BLISS box; a kiss, then the toddler walks in
beats.why: The parcel arrives, with a warm moment.

beats.what: She opens the box and unwraps stacked poufs; the toddler watches
beats.why: The unboxing in one calm static take.

beats.what: The toddler climbs onto a pouf, stands, laughs toward the camera
beats.why: First sight of the set in use.

beats.what: Handheld close-ups: she climbs the arch toward the sofa, smiles at 0:22
Standing on poufs; a hand with a watch steadies her (0:28); she looks at the camera (0:35)
beats.why: More play and a quiet safety cue.

beats.what: Wide shot of the room, poufs and the pink tent
beats.why: Returns to the promise: it looks good.

q2_flow.interaction_prompts: None in the video. The caption is a first-person story with a rhetorical question about the set fitting the living room, but asks nothing.
q2_flow.why: The opening promise is paid off by the closing wide shot of the same room (H5, R4), and the toddler's climbing gives something new every 2 to 6 s (R3). The unboxing take at 0:03 to 0:17 is long and calm, and no voice or Hebrew text says what the set does (R1, H6).

q3_cta.what: None in the video. The caption is a story that opens with 'פוב: כשחשבתי שג'ימבורי זה הדבר שהכי יהרוס לי את הסלון...' and ends 'אני מאוהבת' and '@bliss.il'. No link, code, price or question.
q3_cta.why: No next step: a viewer who wants the set must search the brand tag (C6, C3). The caption gives a reason (a worry turned to love) but no ask. A home-style Reel could earn a send, but nothing says to whom (R5).

q4_shown.what: The finished corner first (arches, poufs, a pink tent) 0:00 to 0:02; a tall BLISS box and a toddler 0:03; stacked poufs unwrapped 0:08; the toddler climbing on poufs and arches 0:12 to 0:35; a hand steadying her at 0:28. No price.
q4_shown.why: Result first, then the box, then play is a fast route to what the caption promises: it fits the living room (S1, K5). The brand shows on the box and as a brief 'By Bliss' (H3). The toddler's face is on camera (S5).

q5_edit.what: About 17 shots in 38 s (2.3 s each): two low pans, one long static unboxing take (0:03 to 0:18), then cuts every 1 to 3 s with closer handheld shots. No speed changes seen. One fixed text. Ends on a wide shot.
q5_edit.why: A slow unboxing then faster cuts of climbing suits calm then energy (E2, R3), though cuts of about 1 s over the toddler's best moments may rush her reaction (E2, K1). It ends on the room with no tail (E8).

q6_topic.what: A pretty foam play corner that does not spoil a living room, via an unboxing and a toddler climbing. Serves a parent who fears gear will ruin her home's look.
q6_topic.why: The worry in the caption, 'a play set will ruin my living room', is a real home concern (K6), answered visually (K5). The toddler's smile at the camera adds warmth (K1). But the idea needs the caption to be understood (H6).

q7_filmed.what: Phone, mostly static: low sweeping pans, a fixed wide shot for the unboxing, then handheld close-ups at the toddler's height and a close-up of a hand steadying her. Bright window light, a tidy cream room. A woman and a toddler.
q7_filmed.why: Low angles and a styled room look like an interior photo, which is the promise (F7), though it reads more polished than homemade (H8). Handheld close-ups keep the toddler large (F4, K8).

q8_text.on_screen: One fixed text for all 38 s, centred at about half the frame height: 'Pov: Your baby's favorite play corner is actually beautiful ✨' in two lines of thin white sans-serif, plus 'By Bliss' at about 65%. English only, no Hebrew subtitles, no CTA. It sits over the toddler's face from about 0:22 to 0:35.
q8_text.caption: 'פוב: כשחשבתי שג'ימבורי זה הדבר שהכי יהרוס לי את הסלון...' A one-paragraph first-person story: the worry, 'ואז גיליתי את בליס והתמכרתי', a question, 'אני מאוהבת', then '@bliss.il'. About 35 words, no hashtags, CTA or disclosure word.
q8_text.why: A single held headline states the idea (T3), but it is English, thin and small on a light picture, and covers the face for a stretch (T5, T2). With no Hebrew text the video says little muted (T1). The caption tells the story in Hebrew but has no hashtags (T7) and no disclosure word (T8).

weak_points: Small thin English text over a light picture and over the child's face; no voice or Hebrew subtitles; no CTA, price or size; no disclosure word; a long calm unboxing before the play.
lumebook_takeaway: A held 'Pov:' headline in Hebrew over the finished result, then the parcel opened in the same room. Hands and the book, no child.
not_verified: Music (the machine 'תודה רבה' only shows no speech). Whether the woman and toddler are the account holder's family. Paid status (label 0, none seen). The name in the caption's question is not quoted. Correction: the unboxing take runs about 0:03 to 0:17, and the headline sits at about half the frame height, so it covers the child's face. Lead edit 18 Oct: resolution remarks removed, because the downloaded copy can be smaller than what was posted.
